systems.system: Nigeria Police Crime and Incident Database Centre (NPCIDB)
systems.country_label: Nigeria Police Crime and Incident Database Centre (NPCIDB)
systems.owner: Nigeria Police Force, which holds it; upgraded by the Federal Ministry of Police Affairs
systems.tiers: the ministry says police document criminals' data through biometrics at Divisional Police Stations across the country and forward it digitally to the NPCIDB, housed in the National Criminal Data Fusion Centre; 'already deployed in the 36 States and the FCT' (as of December 2024)

systems.system: National Criminal Data Fusion Centre (NCDFC) / Data Collection and Registration Centre (DACORE)
systems.country_label: National Criminal Data Fusion Centre (NCDFC), also known as the Data Collection and Registration Centre (DACORE)
systems.owner: Federal Government through the Federal Ministry of Police Affairs
systems.tiers: one national centre, described as now fully functional; a hub collating information on criminal proceedings from law enforcement agencies and sharing the analysis with them

systems.owner: Federal Ministry of Police Affairs; Interpol named as the partner the police work with
systems.tiers: key law enforcement agencies equipped with WAPIS terminals to access information within the year to December 2024, others 'gradually picking up'; more than six training sessions held; nothing said of stations entering cases in it

note: What the ministry describes is biometric capture of criminals' data at divisional stations into a central criminal database, and a fusion centre sharing data among agencies: identification and exchange. It does not say a station enters the report or the case digitally, so no record-class system and no fact, despite the NPCIDB's name; the parent may want to look at the 36 states and FCT claim.
